prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create one extraordinarily polished, fully designed desktop website UI screenshot for Spironolactone Atlas. Landscape frame approximately 1440 by 1080, straight-on edge-to-edge website viewport, no browser chrome and no device frame. This is the first viewport plus a glimpse of the next chapter of a real single-page educational website.

STRUCTURE, in visual order:
A narrow persistent chapter spine on the left, about 120px wide, divided by a thin vertical rule from the reading area. Small typographic brand monogram SA at top. Vertically ordered chapters 01 Overview, 02 Uses, 03 Reports, 04 Evidence, 05 Interactions, 06 Methods. 01 Overview is explicitly active with a coral rule and the word CURRENT. Chapter navigation stays small and quiet.
The main area begins with a compact top navigation line: EDUCATIONAL ATLAS at left, Sources & methods at right. A generous asymmetric editorial title region beneath, not centered. Huge Fraunces-like refined serif title in off-white, two lines: "Spironolactone" and "Atlas". To its right a short readable Inter paragraph: "Uses, evidence and reporting data, read together." Below it a small monospaced label "2004–2025 · SNAPSHOT 3 NOV 2026". Place a coral filled rectangular primary button "Read the story ↓" and a quiet text secondary action "Explore the data ↗". Avoid pill buttons.
A single commanding evidence comparison table spanning almost the entire main area is the focal moment, not a dashboard or cards. Table has generous cell padding, thin horizontal rules, no vertical boxes, aligned columns named "OBSERVATION", "READING", and "LIMIT". Give Observation around 36% width, Reading 31%, Limit 33%. A thin coral rule runs across above the table. Header above table: "Start with what the reports can tell us." in medium editorial serif. The three substantial rows must be aligned and highly readable:
Row 1 observation: "24,805" in large tabular numerals, underneath "selected reports · 2004–2025"; reading: "A defined reporting cohort"; limit: "Reports are not patients."
Row 2 observation: "3,452" in large coral tabular numerals, underneath "hyperkalaemia mentions · 13.9% of selected reports"; reading: "A recorded reaction term"; limit: "Reporting is not incidence or causality."
Row 3 observation: "52.2%" in large teal tabular numerals, underneath "no informative indication"; reading: "Missing information is part of the story"; limit: "Indication data cannot establish prescribing prevalence."
The last row has a restrained horizontal measured bar under its percentage, a visible 52.2% teal portion and remaining portion outlined quietly in off-white, with no decorative chart clutter. This bar is secondary to the table.
Under the table a compact but legible provenance line: "FDA FAERS · selected reports · retrieved 3 Nov 2026" with "View underlying table ↗" at right.
A clearly visible thin-bordered limitation strip in the main reading area reads "Reporting is not incidence or causality." It must feel integrated, precise, not alarmist.
At the lower edge a glimpse of the next chapter: a warm off-white band beginning with small "02 / USES & CONTEXT" then black serif text "One medicine. Different contexts." and a tiny reading arrow. Also show the small line "Educational use only."

DIRECTION:
Journal Club Evidence Table. Clinical journal-club comparison tables expanded into a sophisticated editorial reading surface. Every meaningful number has its interpretation and limit beside it. One dominant focal moment is the huge disciplined table; generous asymmetrical whitespace and decisive headline-to-annotation scale contrast. Academic precision with editorial confidence, readable at first glance. Do not render a grid of cards. Use the full desktop width intelligently.
Palette: near-black clinical ink #0B1020 covers most of viewport, off-white #F3F0E8 text and next-chapter field, coral #F48F7A primary accent and first emphasized value, teal #65B8AC for missing indication. Thin rules in muted off-white. Flat digital surfaces, no gradients. Typography: editorial Fraunces-like serif title and chapter headings, crisp Inter body, JetBrains Mono small annotations and tabular numbers. Table body text is generously sized and readable, not tiny.

REALITY AND CONTENT:
Use the exact product name Spironolactone Atlas. Preserve all provided quantities, dates, denominators and limitation wording exactly. Always reports, never patients as the measured unit. No clinical claims beyond supplied text. No invented findings, prices, percentages, evidence grades, therapy advice, approval labels or validation. Do not add more statistics.
Avoid: glowing molecules, anatomy, organs, SOC maps, medical illustrations, stock patients, photographs, bento cards, decorative floating panels, background grain, fake charts, neon glow, 3D, glossy effects, hero posters, illegible microtext, clipped text, overlapping table cells. Actual excellent website UI, not an art poster.
deviations: Generated frame is 1487 by 1058, close to the requested approximate desktop aspect.
limitations: Planning bitmap preview; final text and responsive behavior require semantic implementation.
